chapter_title: Concerning the Nourishment of the Person, for ther
spiritual_reading:
There is a continual ordered operation that sustains the outward life of a person. Within that outward life there is a vast fullness of distinct confirmations and an equal fullness of governing determinations, so that what is to be received and what is to be directed are both present in sufficient measure. These are successively set into a state fit for reception: what is impure is removed, what is disordered is put into order, and they are admitted inwardly. This is effected through living influx communicated into the outermost degree as doctrine and discernment, and also through a tempering peace that stills lower motions, when the inmost intention turns toward the Divine Source and is held under its presence.

Further, the whole organized set of governing falsities that belong to denial and evil is expelled from that inward domain and cast into instability of state, so that it wanders through successive changes of reception and is displaced from form to form. In this process, some of those falsities are dissolved and carried away by the very changes they undergo, while others are brought back toward order when they can be bent away from opposition and reduced into a subordinate use.

fills.notes: The substrate is describing a continual operation that “exists daily” for the body: an impersonal sustaining function rather than a person or office. “Power” matches the cosmological register (an ordered efficacy) demanded by the spiritual sense (“continual ordered operation that sustains the outward life”).

The clause needs a simple connective to continue the description of what is within the body (seals, rulers). The spiritual sense treats these as paired fullnesses (confirmations and determinations), so coordination is required.
Balances the prior enumeration: the text sets two equal totals (seals; rulers). A simple conjunctive is demanded by the parallelism in the spiritual sense.

After purification they “enter” not merely a place but a degree. The spiritual translation explicitly says “admitted inwardly,” which in the oldest-layer register is best rendered as entering “the Interior” (a discrete degree).

After “enter” a state-word is needed: the spiritual sense speaks of a tempering peace that stills motions. “Rest” is the natural correspondent of that peace and matches the impersonal cosmological tone better than moralized terms.

The sequence “by the voice, by the word, and by the …” calls for a third mode of living influx into ultimates. In the oldest layer, this triad is not ecclesial but correspondential: voice (living utterance), word (discerned doctrine), hymn (ordered sounding that composes and harmonizes). This fits the spiritual sense: influx as doctrine and discernment plus a tempering peace.

The phrase “at the time when his heart … of God the Father” requires a verb of direction/intent, not confession or prayer. The spiritual translation specifies “when the inmost intention turns toward the Divine Source.”

The twelve are a complete organized set of governing falsities; the oldest-layer term is “rulers” (archontic powers). “Great” marks the totality-structure (twelve as a full order) without importing later pastoral language.

The natural expression of “wandering and transmigration” in this substrate is the cyclic re-embodiment schema. “Wheel of births” conveys the instability of state described in the spiritual sense (successive changes of reception, displaced from form to form).

The syntax requires a passive verbal phrase linking “some of them” with the effect of transmigration. The spiritual translation says some falsities are “dissolved and carried away by the very changes they undergo,” which corresponds naturally to being “destroyed through this transmigration.”

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the chapter’s correspondential structure: (1) a continual sustaining power in the outward degree, (2) paired plenitudes (seals and rulers), (3) purification leading to entry into an inner degree and a state of rest, (4) a triadic means of influx (voice, word, ordered sound), and (5) expulsion of a complete archontic order of Darkness into cyclical instability (wandering, transmigration), with differential outcomes (dissolution vs return). Two restorations remain tentative because the exact natural phrasing for the third term after “voice” and “word,” and the specific idiom for transmigration, can vary across recensions.
